title: Ring-theoretic maximum dimension of minimal components below a prime
statement: Let k be a field, S a finite type k-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and p a prime of S with localization S_p and residue field kappa(p) [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], a field extension of k [def-pc-field-extension]. Let d,r be natural numbers with dim S_p=d [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] and trdeg_k kappa(p)=r [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. For every minimal prime q of S contained in p, dim(S/q) <= d+r. There exists such a minimal prime q with dim(S/q)=d+r. Here minimal means q is prime and every prime t contained in q equals q.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Tag 00P1, lines 28238-28267: the prime-chain calculation, excluding the appeal to Tag 00OT for topological dimension.

proof.text: Apply the auxiliary finite-component form of the prime-chain argument, which supplies a finite set qs of exactly the minimal primes below p, bounds all quotient dimensions by d+r, and attains the bound.

mathlib_searches.query: For a finite type algebra over a field, the maximum dimension of quotients by minimal primes below p equals the dimension of the localization at p plus the transcendence degree of its residue field
The maximum of the dimensions of S/q for minimal primes q contained in p equals dim S_p plus trdeg k kappa(p) for a finite type k-algebra S

theorem minimal_component_dimension_maximum
    {k : Type u} [Field k] {S : Type v} [CommRing S] [Algebra k S]
    [Algebra.FiniteType k S] (p : Ideal S) [p.IsPrime]
    (d r : ℕ)
    (hd : ringKrullDim (Localization.AtPrime p) = (d : WithBot ℕ∞))
    (hr : Algebra.trdeg k p.ResidueField = (r : Cardinal.{v})) :
    (∀ q : Ideal S, q.IsPrime → q ≤ p →
      (∀ t : Ideal S, t.IsPrime → t ≤ q → t = q) →
      ringKrullDim (S ⧸ q) ≤ ((d + r : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞)) ∧
    (∃ q : Ideal S, q.IsPrime ∧ q ≤ p ∧
      (∀ t : Ideal S, t.IsPrime → t ≤ q → t = q) ∧
      ringKrullDim (S ⧸ q) = ((d + r : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞))
